content.why_desc: Regular expressions (regex) are powerful pattern-matching tools used in nearly every programming language. Debugging regex can be challenging — a single wrong character changes the entire match behavior. Our real-time regex tester highlights matches as you type, shows capture group details, and supports all JavaScript regex flags, making it the fastest way to build and validate your patterns.

live.title: Live Match Highlighting
live.desc: See matches highlighted in real-time as you type — no need to press any button

groups.title: Capture Group Details
groups.desc: View all capture groups, their indices, and matched values for each match

flags.title: Full Flag Support
flags.desc: Toggle g, i, m, s, u, y flags independently and see how they affect matches instantly

content.how_title: How to Test Regex in 3 Steps

1.title: Enter Your Pattern
1.desc: Type your regular expression in the pattern field (without surrounding slashes)

2.title: Select Flags
2.desc: Toggle g (global), i (case-insensitive), m (multiline) and other flags as needed

3.title: Paste Test String
3.desc: Enter the text to test against — matches will be highlighted automatically

validation.title: Form Validation

search.title: Text Search & Replace
search.desc: Find and replace patterns in code editors, log files, and text processing pipelines

parsing.title: Log File Parsing

anchor.title: ✓ Use Anchors for Exact Matches
anchor.desc: Use ^ and $ to anchor patterns to the start and end of a string, preventing partial matches

groups.title: ✓ Use Non-Capturing Groups When Possible
groups.desc: Use (?:...) instead of (...) when you don't need to capture the group, improving performance

escape.title: ✓ Escape Special Characters
escape.desc: Characters like . * + ? ( ) [ ] { } | ^ $ \ have special meaning — escape with \ when you want literal matches

test.title: ✓ Test Edge Cases
test.desc: Always test with empty strings, Unicode characters, very long inputs, and boundary conditions

faq.q1: What regex flavor does this tester use?
faq.a1: This tester uses JavaScript's built-in RegExp engine, which follows the ECMAScript standard. It supports all JS regex features including lookaheads, lookbehinds (ES2018+), named capture groups, and Unicode property escapes.
faq.q2: What's the difference between the g and m flags?
faq.a2: The g (global) flag finds all matches in the string instead of just the first one. The m (multiline) flag makes ^ and $ match the start/end of each line rather than the entire string. They serve different purposes and can be combined.
faq.q3: How do I match a literal dot or asterisk?
faq.a3: Escape them with a backslash: \. matches a literal dot, \* matches a literal asterisk. In a character class [ ], most special characters lose their special meaning, except ] \ ^ -.
faq.q4: Why does my regex match too much?
faq.a4: You're likely using greedy quantifiers. The * and + quantifiers are greedy by default and match as much as possible. Add ? to make them lazy: *? or +? will match as little as possible.
